text: Hydrogen burns in oxygen to make water. Write it down and count the atoms on each side. Something does not add up. Can you spot it? Count the oxygen atoms on each side. Which side is short? Atoms are never created or destroyed in a reaction, so each element must have the same count on both sides. Left side, two hydrogen and two oxygen. Right side, two hydrogen and one oxygen. Oxygen is short on the right. Put a two in front of hydrogen and a two in front of water. A tempting fix is to change a subscript, so water becomes hydrogen peroxide. The counts can match, but that is a different compound. Only coefficients may change. Balance by changing coefficients, never subscripts. Two hydrogen molecules and one oxygen molecule give two water molecules. Four hydrogen and two oxygen on each side. AI-generated narration. Script by Examleaf.
